entries.payment_processor: Utility consolidated billing in most states; in-house for CA/GA/TX
entries.notes: If XOOM appears on your utility bill (most states), keep paying the utility. XOOM bills directly only in California (SDG&E/SoCalGas areas), Georgia and Texas: pay online in MyXOOM, by phone (Texas 833-355-9666, Georgia 855-203-3808, California 888-997-8979), by mail (Texas: XOOM Energy Texas, LLC, P.O. Box 660133, Dallas, TX 75266-0133; CA/GA: Accounts Receivable, P.O. Box 650411, Dallas, TX 75265-0411) or in cash (Texas: Barri, CheckFree, Fidelity Express; CA/GA: ACE, Walmart). Auto-Bill Pay: set up from the MyXOOM dashboard ('Set up Auto Bill Pay'; starts with the next bill), change or cancel under 'Manage Auto Bill Pay', or call Customer Care. Paperless Billing (CA/GA/TX): enroll in MyAccount or by phone. Budget and average billing pages: xoomenergy.com/en/budget-billing and /en/average-billing. To cancel: Contact Us form ('Cancel Account') or 888-997-8979 (Mon-Fri 8am-11pm, Sat 9am-7pm ET); term plans may carry an early termination (cost recovery) fee - see xoomenergy.com/en/cancel-account. Texas: the REP sends the bill; the delivery utility (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) only handles wires and outages. Ask for a payment extension or deferred payment plan before the due date; call 2-1-1 (211texas.org) for local bill-help agencies. Seniors and people with serious medical conditions can apply for critical care / chronic condition status for extra disconnection protection. Outside Texas the supplier is usually billed through the local utility (utility consolidated billing): the supply charge is a line on the utility bill, so view, pay, set up or stop autopay, see history and get help (LIHEAP, budget billing, senior/low-income discounts, PIPP/PCAP) through the utility. Call the supplier about the rate, contract, renewal or cancellation; returning to the utility's default service takes 1-2 billing cycles, and fixed-rate contracts may carry an early termination fee (see the contract summary).

entries.notes: Outside Texas and Georgia most Constellation home customers see the charge on their utility bill and pay the utility. Direct-billed customers: Payment Options page covers online payment in the Constellation account (account.constellation.com) or as a guest (Paymentus), free pay by phone (Texas 833-221-6654, Georgia 844-508-3525, all other markets 833-370-0594), mail to Constellation, P.O. Box 5471, Carol Stream, IL 60197-5471, and cash via MoneyGram. Autopay is set up in the online account (agents cannot do it for you); cancel it with the Cancel Autopay button before 9pm ET the day before the scheduled draft. The Online Account FAQ covers bills, payment history and account settings in the new online account. Cancel service by calling Customer Care (Texas 888-900-7052, Mon-Fri 7am-8pm, Sat 8am-5pm CT; Georgia 877-677-4355; all others 855-465-1244, Mon-Fri 8am-8pm ET); fixed-term contracts may carry a cancellation fee. Home Services (HVAC/plumbing plans) have separate numbers. Texas: the REP sends the bill; the delivery utility (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) only handles wires and outages. Ask for a payment extension or deferred payment plan before the due date; call 2-1-1 (211texas.org) for local bill-help agencies. Seniors and people with serious medical conditions can apply for critical care / chronic condition status for extra disconnection protection. Outside Texas the supplier is usually billed through the local utility (utility consolidated billing): the supply charge is a line on the utility bill, so view, pay, set up or stop autopay, see history and get help (LIHEAP, budget billing, senior/low-income discounts, PIPP/PCAP) through the utility. Call the supplier about the rate, contract, renewal or cancellation; returning to the utility's default service takes 1-2 billing cycles, and fixed-rate contracts may carry an early termination fee (see the contract summary).

Texas: the REP sends the bill; the delivery utility (Oncor, CenterPoint, AEP Texas, TNMP) only handles wires and outages. Ask for a payment extension or deferred payment plan before the due date; call 2-1-1 (211texas.org) for local bill-help agencies. Seniors and people with serious medical conditions can apply for critical care / chronic condition status for extra disconnection protection. Outside Texas the supplier is usually billed through the local utility (utility consolidated billing): the supply charge is a line on the utility bill, so view, pay, set up or stop autopay, see history and get help (LIHEAP, budget billing, senior/low-income discounts, PIPP/PCAP) through the utility. Call the supplier about the rate, contract, renewal or cancellation; returning to the utility's default service takes 1-2 billing cycles, and fixed-rate contracts may carry an early termination fee (see the contract summary).
